author: TEDx Talks
description:
We all know what gambling looks like - right? But gambling isn't as simple as it appears on the surface. In an age where you can bet on anything and everything, understanding what it really means to gamble, and recognizing it when you're doing it, is more important than ever. 

Gillian is an assistant research professor in the Penn State Abington Criminal Justice Research Center. Gillian holds a BSc in Psychology from the University of British Columbia Okanagan, an MSc in Psychology from the University of Lethbridge, and is completing her PhD in Evolution and Behaviour at the University of Lethbridge. Her research has primarily focused on how cognitions influence addictive behaviors, with a particular focus on gambling. Through Penn State she is currently managing the Interactive Gaming Assessment, a legislated annual assessment of the impacts of legalized online gambling in Pennsylvania. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized
title: Have you been gambling without realizing it? | Gillian Russell | TEDxPSU

author: TEDx Talks
description: In this talk, Darren Radford reframes artificial intelligence not as a threat to humanity but as a catalyst for human potential. Drawing from his experience as a university professor, he shows how AI can take over mundane, time-consuming tasks like grading so humans can focus on what they do best: teaching, healing, creating, and connecting. Darren argues that fear-driven narratives about AI replacing jobs obscure a more powerful possibility: AI freeing people from administrative overload and amplifying human creativity and compassion. From education to healthcare, he invites us to shift the question from “What will AI take?” to “What could it make possible?” By choosing curiosity over fear, he urges us to use this moment to reimagine work, purpose, and what it truly means to be human. Darren is a purpose-driven leader, strategy and business transformation specialist who helps organizations build strategic agility for a fast-moving world. Beginning his career as a lawyer in the U.K.,
title: AI Won’t Replace You: It’s Here to Liberate You | Darren Radford | TEDxSurrey

author: TEDx Talks
description: In this talk, Hargun Dhillon shares how his grandfather’s struggle to stay active after heart surgery revealed a deeper problem in how we design “healthy” spaces. Living in one of the world’s healthiest regions, his Punjabi-speaking grandfather still couldn’t find a fitness program that felt welcoming or culturally safe. Hargun maintains the issue isn’t motivation but belonging. Through starting a small, community-based fitness group rooted in language, culture, and connection, he shows how equity not one-size-fits-all solutions create real health outcomes. The talk reframes fitness as a social and cultural experience, demonstrating that true wellbeing comes from community, compassion, and designing spaces where people feel seen. Hargun is an award-winning University of British Columbia kinesiology student, community health advocate, and founder of Age Strong Unity Wellness Society—a youth-led, culturally tailored fitness nonprofit for seniors. What began with a few dumbbells in a Sur
title: The Hidden Barrier Keeping Seniors from Fitness | Hargun Dhillon | TEDxSurrey

author: TEDx Talks
description: In this talk, Jessi Beyer contends that our biggest problems are rarely solved by choosing sides but by pairing opposing perspectives. She opens with a tense 911 call involving a man experiencing psychosis who believed there was a bomb in his van, showing how collaboration between law enforcement and mental health professionals led to a safe outcome neither could have achieved alone. From this experience, she expands to a broader critique of society’s addiction to extremes amplified by tribal instincts and social media algorithms. Jessi makes the case that progress comes from nuance, curiosity, and cooperation, urging us to replace “either/or” thinking with intentional collaboration, especially beyond moments of crisis. Jessi is the #1 best-selling author of How To Heal: A Practical Guide to Nine Integrative Therapies That Can Help Release Trauma. She is a crisis mental health clinician with two law enforcement agencies and three fire departments in Washington State and a negotiator w
title: How to Think Outside Your Own Box | Jessi Beyer | TEDxSurrey

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this talk, Lei Wang uses a gruelling ski expedition to the South Pole to reframe boredom as a powerful signal rather than a problem. In the endless, silent white of Antarctica, Lei discovers that the real danger isn’t the cold or physical strain, but mental drift caused by monotony, nearly leading to hypothermia. By learning to work with repetition rather than escape it, she turns boredom into focused engagement, setting small goals that restore attention and momentum. That mindset later sparks creative breakthroughs that improve future expeditions. She argues that in life’s long, repetitive stretches, boredom is an invitation to re-engage. When we respond with intention, monotony becomes a training ground for focus, resilience, and unexpected creativity. From Wall Street to the world’s tallest peaks, Lei Wang has learned that greatness isn’t forged in moments of thrill—it’s built through steady, intentional pursuit. 

A Wharton-trained former finance professional turned leadership
title: How to make boredom your superpower | Lei Wang | TEDxSurrey

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this powerful and deeply personal talk, David Patrick Farrell shares his journey from a childhood of fear, violence, and addiction in a Dublin council estate to a life of recovery, purpose, and connection. Growing up without emotional safety, Farrell learned early that vulnerability was dangerous, leading him down a path of drugs, crime, and despair.

Through honesty, courage, and the transformative power of men’s communities, he discovered that what many men are truly seeking is not strength or bravado but belonging, acceptance, and a space to be human. Farrell shows how loneliness, not malice, often underlies violence, addiction, and anger, and argues that by creating safe spaces for men to share and be seen, we can break cycles of harm, strengthen families, and build healthier communities.

This talk is a call to action: a reminder that none of us are meant to carry life alone and that healing begins when we are witnessed, heard, and connected. David Patrick Farrell is a global
title: Men’s work: A shared journey | David Patrick Farrell | TEDxUWS

His technical background includes engineering secure architecture for the UK’s primary defense research organization and developing award-winning algorithmic solutions for a tier-one global investment bank.

As a specialist in Cybersecurity and Digital Forensics, Atanas’s work ranges from securing critical infrastructure to developing intelligent, cooperative systems for autonomous technology. title: The Power of Doing: Why Action Beats Theory | Atanas Burmov | TEDxBournemouth University

This talk dives into how personal branding, digital presence, and positioning shape opportunities. If you’ve ever felt overlooked despite your abilities, this talk will change how you think about growth, attention, and showing up in the modern world. author: TEDx Talks
description:
Ahmed Berramdane introduces a simple but powerful idea: most of us don’t struggle with knowing what to do; we struggle with actually doing it. In a world filled with hesitation, overthinking, and the pressure to be perfect, action often feels like the hardest step.

Using the D.A.N.G.E.R. system, Ahmed outlines a practical method for moving forward despite fear. This approach emphasizes the importance of starting small, assuming kindness, noticing the moment, moving forward despite fear, choosing enthusiasm over perfection, and repeating the process.

This is not about having it all figured out. It’s about starting where you are, embracing uncertainty, and learning to act even when it feels uncomfortable.

If you’ve ever felt stuck, delayed your goals, or waited for the “right time,” this talk will challenge you to rethink how progress really happens.

Because occasionally, the most powerful thing you can do is go anyway. Ahmed Berramdane is a Chevening Scholar and MSc candidate in Me
title: The D.A.N.G.E.R. system for doing hard things | Ahmed Berramdane | TEDxBournemouth University

author: TEDx Talks
description: After Hurricane Katrina destroyed his home, researcher Daniel Aldrich spent years studying thousands of disaster survivors across four continents to find out what actually determines meaningful recovery. Among the observations after the 2011 earthquake and tsunami in Japan, some communities lost one in ten people while neighboring communities experienced no fatalities. Data showed the difference was not money, not infrastructure, and not government response. It was whether people knew their neighbors. Aldrich investigates why greater social connections are correlated with higher survival, evacuation, and mental health recovery rates after disaster. He makes a practical case for the specific policies and habits that build those connections before the next shock arrives. Daniel P. Aldrich is Dean's Professor of Resilience and Co-Director of the Global Resilience Institute at Northeastern University, where he holds appointments in Political Science, Public Policy, and Urban Affairs. He i
title: Studying recoveries after disasters showed a clear protective factor | Daniel Aldrich | TEDxBoston

author: TEDx Talks
description: 700 million people already live with food insecurity, and the world needs 70% more food by 2050. The resource-hungry synthetic fertilizers that power modern agriculture consume 2% of all global energy to produce nitrogen-based fertilizers alone. An MIT lab found a solution in an unlikely place: crustacean shells. A coating made from seafood waste can deliver beneficial soil microbes directly into the ground at planting, with no refrigeration, no new supply chain, and no synthetic inputs. In trials in Morocco, seeds treated this way are growing faster and more nutritiously on land previously too degraded to farm. Benedetto Marelli is Associate Professor in the Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering at MIT, where he directs the Laboratory for Advanced Biopolymers. His research focuses on structural biopolymers, self-assembly, and nanomanufacturing, with applications in precision agriculture, food security, and food safety. He is the recipient of the Presidential Early Career
title: Is the key to feeding 10 billion people already in the trash? | Benedetto Marelli | TEDxBoston

author: TEDx Talks
description: When is the last time you battled a pothole? Modern concrete crumbles in decades, while Roman aqueducts built 2,000 years ago are still standing strong. Research at MIT discovered a secret in the ancient mixing process: calcium-rich pockets embedded in the material that dissolve and fill cracks over time. That insight is driving a new generation concrete that heals itself, absorbs carbon, and stores electricity. The stakes are high. Concrete is the most produced material on Earth, accounting for 8% of global CO2 emissions. Meanwhile, the world needs to keep building exponentially to house a growing population. Learn how material scientists are unlocking incredible properties in multifunctional construction materials to build cities of the future.  Admir Masic is Associate Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering at MIT, where he directs the Masic Lab and serves as a principal investigator at the MIT Concrete Sustainability Hub. A physical chemist by training, he holds an MSc a
title: What 2,000-year-old concrete can teach us about building the future | Admir Masic | TEDxBoston

author: TEDx Talks
description: The US recently set a record for the number of multi-billion dollar extreme weather disasters in a single two-year period. Instead of costly, reactive responses, every dollar invested in disaster preparedness today can save up to $33 in future losses. One urban planning expert argues this can be done, beautifully, by weaving resilience into the fabric of a city through the foundational principle of dual-use. City sctructures designed to both delight for everyday life and serve the moment disaster strikes. A park that serves as a flood basin, a community bench that doubles as a solar charger, a BBQ pit that becomes an emergency hub... this is what the future of resilient cities could look like.   Miho Mazereeuw is Associate Professor of Architecture and Urbanism and Director of the Urban Risk Lab at MIT, where she also serves as MIT Climate Mission Lead for Empowering Frontline Communities and Associate Head for Strategy and Equity in the Department of Architecture. Trained as both an
title: What if every park, bench, and building was also a disaster tool? | Miho Mazereeuw | TEDxBoston

description:
This is a deeply personal exploration shared by Olympic medalist Sakshi Malik about her journey from a small- town girl with an unattainable dream to the Olympic podium and the unseen self that existed beneath it all. She shared that growing up in  surroundings where wrestling was considered a “boys’ sport”, Sakshi faced numerous challenges; financial constraints, career-threatening injuries, societal resistance, and crushing self- doubt. 

But this talk goes beyond medals and victories. Sakshi reveals the identity she constructed to survive, the parts of herself she had to silence to succeed, and the vulnerability she eventually embraced as strength. Through moments of retrospective clarity, she examines the internal conflicts that truly shaped her - the battles fought not on the mat, but within.

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Depuis des décennies, deux clans s'affrontent pour essayer d’analyser le monde : les **Rationalistes**, partisans de la logique pure, et les **Empiristes**, qui ne jurent que par l'observation des données. Si les premiers ont longtemps dominé jusqu’à la victoire de Deep Blue sur Garry Kasparov, nous vivons aujourd'hui le triomphe absolu des seconds grâce au Deep Learning.

Mais comment en est-on arrivé là ? Nous découvrons comment une "loterie hardware" — l'utilisation détournée des puces de jeux vidéo comme celles de Mario Galaxy*— a provoqué un séisme technologique en 2012. Pourtant, malgré les milliards investis et les scénarios de science-fiction, l'IA actuelle possède un talon d'Achille majeur : elle excelle dans la corrélation, mais reste "à côté de la plaque" dès qu'il s'agit de comprendre les relations de causalité.

Pourquoi devrions-nous arrêter d'attendre un miracle ? À travers l'exemple concret d'un chef d'atelier cherchant à optimiser sa production, Mehdi Mounsif propose
title: L'IA, une technologie de plus dans la boîte à outils | Mehdi MOUNSIF | TEDxClermont

description: What can music tell us about the lives that hatred and history almost erased? During the Holocaust, composers and musicians created works under unimaginable conditions while imprisoned in ghettos or concentration camps. Their music expressed hope, beauty, pain and resilience – an affirmation of life in the midst of darkness. Maestro Francesco Lotoro blends historical research with live performance, uncovering the stories hidden in these scores and revealing how music became both a tool of survival and a testament to humanity. This talk is a journey into memory, emotion, and the enduring power of art even in the darkest times. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

description:
Leadership is not about authority. It is about empathy. Kyara shares how leading with compassion and authenticity can create lasting impact, even through the smallest actions. In a world focused on outcomes, this talk reminds us that how we lead matters most. As a student at the University of Auckland, Kyara has been involved in several leadership positions, which have ignited her interest in understanding what it means to be a leader. 

In her talk, Kyara will explore leadership from a new perspective. Not as a title worn by a selected few, but as a choice everyone can make in their daily lives. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Small Steps, Big Ripples: Leading with the Heart | Kyara Wiriadinata | TEDxUOA

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the world could speak a shared language. Not just in words, but in understanding? Through the story of Esperanto, Cameron explores humanity’s long-standing desire for connection beyond borders. This talk reveals how language shapes not only communication, but the way we relate to one another. Cameron has been interested in the power of languages and communication throughout his life - whether it be the language of music, creative writing, or constructed languages like Esperanto.

Cameron will speak on how, despite Esperanto being a constructed language, the culture and community created around it exemplifies the experience and benefits of learning any language. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Can One Language Bring Us Together? | Cameron Burton | TEDxUOA

author: TEDx Talks
description: Laughter and creativity transformed a dying church into a thriving community in less than two years—what bold, creative step could spark a breakthrough in your own life? Father Spencer Reece graduated from Wesleyan where he studied with Annie Dillard. Reece went on to York University in the UK and Harvard Divinity. A Guggenheim Fellow, Reece’s first manuscript, The Clerk’s Tale, was selected for the Bakeless Prize by Nobel Laureate Louise Glück. James Franco made a film from the title poem. Reece returned to seminary at Yale, in mid-life and was ordained in Madrid, Spain, in 2011. He was awarded a Fulbright to teach poetry at Our Little Roses in San Pedro, Honduras, where he lived and worked with the girls at the orphanage. The work was made into an award-winning film, Voices Beyond the Wall: 12 Love Poems from the Murder Capital of the World. He moved to Madrid and assisted the Episcopal Bishop of Spain for a decade. His third book of poems Acts was published in May of 2024. In 2025,
title: Hark: How laughter saved a church | Spencer Reece | TEDxURI

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Identität wird oft in Kategorien gedacht. Immer wieder sehen wir nicht den Menschen als komplexes Individuum, sondern nur seine Herkunft, seine sexuelle Orientierung, oder seine Behinderung. Aber es gibt eine universelle Sprache, die sämtliche Schubladen öffnet und Perspektivwechsel ermöglicht: Humor. 

Auf der Bühne von TEDxMünster teilt Okan Seese exemplarische Anekdoten aus seinem Alltag als türkisch-deutscher, schwuler und tauber Comedian. Statt Missverständnisse, Vorurteile und Konflikte zu umschiffen, macht er sie pointiert sichtbar und beweist auf diese Weise die produktive Kraft von Humor. Denn wer gemeinsam lacht, begegnet sich auf Augenhöhe. Okan Seese ist taub, schwul, türkischstämmig – und einer der spannendsten Comedians Deutschlands. Auf der Bühne zeigt er, wie Humor Brücken schlägt und Menschen verbindet. Mit Witz, Charme und einer guten Portion Selbstironie erzählt Okan Seese von seinem Leben zwischen den Welten und davon, wie man Klischees mit einem Augenzwinkern spre
title: Missverständnis inklusive: Über die Komplexität von Kommunikation | Okan Seese | TEDxMünster Salon

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Was bedeutet eigentlich Erfolg? 

Schon in der Schule unterscheiden wir zwischen förderfähigen und förderbedürftigen Kindern, zwischen High Performern und Nachzüglern. Zahlen und Rankings scheinen objektive Leistungsbeurteilungen zu ermöglichen. Doch was, wenn sich unsere Gesellschaft nach den falschen Maßstäben richtet?

Nadine Schönwald stellt unser Verständnis von Wert grundlegend infrage. Als Führungskraft in einem Weltkonzern und als eine Frau mit Schwerbehinderung hat sie in ihrem Leben wiederholt sämtlichen Erwartungen ihres Umfeldes getrotzt. So hat sie einen vielfältigen Blick auf das Konzept von ‘Leistung’ gewonnen und fordert nun auch uns heraus, unsere Weltanschauung zu überdenken und uns nicht länger auf das zu konzentrieren, was sich in Kennzahlen erfassen lässt.  Nadine Schönwald packt dort an, wo es wichtig ist. Als Führungskraft mit Schwerbehinderung und Head of Sales Support bei The Adecco Group setzt sie sich mit Leidenschaft für Chancengleichheit, Barrierefreiheit
title: Die Leistungslüge | Nadine Schönwald | TEDxMünster Salon

author: TEDx Talks
description: Moving every few years makes it hard to fit into a cultural box. Lyla Belnap’s solution? Build your own. From "Hamburger Nights" to family video rituals, Lyla explains how to construct a "Custom-Built Culture" that creates stability in a world of constant motion. Her challenge to the audience: don't just inherit culture—create it. Lyla Belnap is a 13-year-old Grade 8 student at the American School of Madrid. A Chinese-American originally from Salt Lake City, Utah, she brings a unique perspective as the middle sibling between an older brother and a younger sister. An adventurer at heart who is always up for trying new things, Lyla has embraced her life in Spain and is excited to step onto the TEDx stage to share her ideas. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: My Custom Built Culture | Lyla Xiao Yi Zhen Belnap | TEDxASM Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: Why do we defend beliefs even when facts prove us wrong? It’s called "Motivated Reasoning." Paz Garcia-Blanch dives into the psychology of how our brains filter reality to protect our worldview. By understanding this "illogical logic," she shows how we can stop defending our egos and start turning cultural clashes into opportunities for connection. Paz was born in New York and moved to Madrid in 2021. Currently a Grade 10 student at the American School of Madrid, she describes herself as an aspiring philosopher. Paz loves asking difficult questions about the world and the people in it—a curiosity that led her to discover the incredible phenomenon of motivated reasoning, which she will be exploring in her talk. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: How Our Own Reasoning Can Deceive Us in Everyday Life | Paz Garcia-Blanch Echeverria | TEDxASM Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
艾诚的职业轨迹横跨北京大学、哈佛大学、中央电视台驻纽约财经评论员到创业者，她长期记录这个时代的创新者与变革者。然而，一次深刻的人生告别经历让她重新审视"被看见"的真正含义——被看见的不应仅仅是那些站在聚光灯下的时代创新者，更应包括那些在日常生活中默默照亮他人的普通人。当人工智能以前所未有的速度改变世界、重构产业与职业时，她选择重新站上舞台，重启真人深度访谈项目，决心记录那些不可被算法计算、无法被数据量化的人性之光。她提出，AI技术或许能够决定我们奔跑的速度与效率，但只有人类内心深处的爱、同理心与道德选择，才能决定我们奔跑的方向与终点。在技术的狂飙突进中，她呼吁让"人"的核心价值重新被看见、被珍视。Ai Cheng’s career trajectory spans from Peking University and Harvard University to serving as a financial commentator for CCTV in New York, and later becoming an entrepreneur. For years, she has documented the innovators and changemakers of our time.
Yet a deeply personal experience of farewell led her to reexamine the true meaning of “being seen.” To her, visibility should not belong only to those standing under the spotlight, but also to the ordinary individuals who quietly illuminate the lives of others.
As artificial intelligence reshapes the world, industries, and professions at an unprecedented pace, she chose to return to the stage and relaunch her in-depth human interview project
title: 在AI时代，让"人"重新被看见 In the age of AI, Le's see people again | 艾诚  | TEDxHongqiao Women

author: TEDx Talks
description:
A child's future can hinge on what we notice, or what we overlook, in the first few years of life. Yet too often, we “wait and see”, instead of properly measuring a child’s developmental progress over time and - if needed - acting early. 

This talk reveals why early detection - empowered by parent-centred screening tools - can positively transform a child's future. The take home point is to dramatically improve early detection and intervention services for young children.   MD, PhD, paediatrician This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

 Alisa has spent more than three decades in oncology, beginning her career as a bedside oncology nurse.
